investigation.scenes_py_timeline_reference: pipeline/stage_a/scenes.py detect_shots() runs `ffmpeg -i <video> -filter:v select='gt(scene,T)',showinfo` and parses pts_time fields (lines 42-80). Per stage-a.yml lines 448-452, `scenes all` is invoked on $ORIGINAL_PATH = jobs/<id>/ingest.json's original_path = work/original.<ext> (the ingested source, NOT a re-encoded copy — bug-68 removed the 720p analysis copy entirely; bundle.py lines 18/186 confirm analysis_720p.mp4 is no longer produced). pts_time values are the ORIGINAL source container's own presentation timestamps, zero-based from source start. Baseline composites extract_baseline_composites() (lines 519-566) also run on the same original: fps=1,tile=3x2 -> grid_NNNNN.jpg renamed to frame_<seq*6>.jpg, so frame_000042.jpg = source seconds [42,48). Event composites emit_event_composite() seek with input-side `-ss <center-2> -t 4 -i <original>` (lines 380-404), same reference. CONCLUSION: scenes/screenshot timeline = original source video timeline, zero offset, no resample/trim between.
investigation.transcript_timeline_reference: stage-a.yml lines 434-438: `ffmpeg -y -i $ORIGINAL_PATH -vn -ac 1 -ar 16000 -c:a pcm_s16le work/audio.wav` then transcribe work/audio.wav. Same $ORIGINAL_PATH as scenes. The -vn/-ac/-ar re-encode extracts audio starting at source t=0 with no seek/trim, so the WAV is 1:1 time-locked to the source. faster-whisper transcribe() (transcribe.py lines 188-197) returns segment start/end on that WAV's timeline = original source timeline. transcribe_to_json persists audio_duration_seconds = last segment end (lines 260,280). CONCLUSION: transcript timeline = original source timeline, SAME reference as scenes.py. No offset between them.
investigation.renderpy_extraction_reference: pipeline/stage_b/render.py produce_merged_video() line 309: for each cut emits `-ss {start_seconds:.3f} -to {end_seconds:.3f} -i <src>` where src=original_video (the same ingested source re-obtained by Stage B). Input-side seek against the ORIGINAL source timeline. render_merged() line 617 probes src_duration = common.probe_duration_seconds(original_video) (ffprobe format=duration). Lines 663-676 validate each reconciled cut range against [0, src_duration+0.5]. setpts stretch (line 327) only retimes, never moves boundaries. CONCLUSION: render extraction timeline = original source timeline, SAME reference. The three producers/consumers (scenes, transcript, render) all agree on the original source timeline.
investigation.automatic_py_offset_check: pipeline/plan/automatic.py: the model reads transcript.json, scene_index.json, key_moments.json via tools and opens screenshot composites. composite_window_seconds() (lines 238-251) maps frame_NNNNNN.jpg -> [N, N+window) and event_MMMMMMMMM.jpg -> [center-2, center+2] using the SAME zero-based source-time the filenames encode (matches scenes.py naming). visual_grounding_errors() (lines 649-682) requires each cut's start/end to be covered by opened composite windows, enforcing that chosen seconds correspond to visually-confirmed source moments. No additive/subtractive offset is applied anywhere to start_seconds/end_seconds in automatic.py; seconds are taken verbatim from the evidence. CONCLUSION: no systematic offset in automatic.py's mapping.
investigation.test_case_result: Constructed test in pipeline/tests/test_scene_accuracy.py: built a synthetic 12s source whose every one-second span is a distinct solid color (second N = known RGB), ran a cut [4s,7s] through the REAL render_merged() with a 2.4s voiceover (80% ratio, above the 75% collapse floor), and verified by decoding output frames with Pillow: output duration 2.42s (footage sped up 3.0s->2.4s exactly), first output frame = source second 4 color, near-end output frame (t=2.30s) = source second 6 color. Frame selection is EXACTLY the requested source range — confirming timelines are consistent and render.py's extraction/setpts is correct. The duration-guard unit tests confirm the fix: declared 9283s vs actual 1379s now fails loudly naming both durations and 'wrong scene'; sub-2s rounding differences pass.
investigation.confirmed_root_cause: Missing declared-vs-actual source-duration sanity check (investigation candidate 5). production.json's video_duration_seconds is the planner's whole reference for every cut's start/end seconds, and the schema validator only checks cuts' end_seconds <= video_duration_seconds, while Stage B render only checks cuts against the REAL probed duration — NOTHING ever compared the declared duration to the actual probed duration of the file being rendered. If the two diverge (stale plan, wrong/older source re-fetched via bug-69 refetch_source.py, source edited/replaced between Stage A and Stage B, or a hallucinated/wrong duration in a manual plan), every start_seconds/end_seconds is interpreted against a different-length timeline than the planner used, so cuts land on entirely the wrong scene while passing both validators — exactly the operator's symptom. All timeline producers/consumers themselves are consistent (candidates 1-4 ruled out with code evidence + the constructed frame-fidelity test). For the reported job manual-1788116412985 (declared 9283s, cuts 7028-8162s, single-file torrent whose one candidate 2908144950 bytes == ingest.json size_bytes so Stage A and Stage B necessarily used the same MKV) the bug is latent/structural rather than proven for that specific file — but the missing guard is the concrete defect that lets the symptom occur silently.

The 2 failures + 6 errors in the full suite (ReframeDetectionTierTests opencv/yolo cascade bundle availability, WriteStatusTests terminal-state test requiring CI env) are PRE-EXISTING on the pristine base commit 9dbf814 (verified by running the suite on a clean clone: identical 8 failures, 265 tests) and are unrelated to this change.

fix.approach: Added render.assert_declared_duration_matches_source(plan, actual_seconds) in pipeline/stage_b/render.py with SOURCE_DURATION_MISMATCH_TOLERANCE_S = 2.0 (absorbs integer rounding of the ffprobe value; ffprobe container duration is accurate to well under 1s). Called in render_merged() immediately after src_duration is probed (line ~617) and before any reconciliation/render work, so a plan whose declared video_duration_seconds disagrees with the actual source duration by >2s fails closed with a StageBError naming both durations, the delta, and the remediation (re-run Stage A against this exact source and regenerate the plan). Wired into the single choke point: render_merged is called by pipeline.stage_b.run (the orchestrator) after boundary validation, so every render path — manual plans, automatic plans, series parts — is guarded. Timeline contract documented in ARCHITECTURE.md §7.3.1.
